newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IBM sees strong telecom business in Asia.
newsitem.headline: IBM sees strong telecom business in Asia.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp (IBM) said on Wednesday its telecommunications and media business was likely to go on growing at double-digit rates in the Asia-Pacific region.

"Our telecommunications and media business in Asia Pacific grew 70 percent faster than the market did in 1996 and we expect it to continue at a double-digit growth," James Steele, IBM's Asia Pacific general manager for telecommunications and media industries, told a news conference.
He declined to reveal revenue figures but said telecoms and media was the third largest out of the 12 industries IBM has carved its business into, behind banking and finance and manufacturing.

Steele said deregulation of the telecoms industry the Asia-Pacifi region was providing losts of opportunities for IBM. So was the technology convergence between information providers, telecoms companies and information technology companies, he said.
Steele said the value of hardware, software and services sold to the telecoms and media market was expected to reach US$9 billion in 1997 after growing at a "high single digit" rate.
"I don't see any slow down. In the next three to five years, this market should be the fastest in terms of geography and in terms of the industry," he said.

Steele said IBM had many competitors in various niche markets in the region but none could provide the "end-to-end" solutions comprising hardware, software, services and skills to understand different customer needs that IBM did.
